user_query: My father had a stroke and can't manage his affairs. How do I help?
variations: Parent lost mental capacity, what do I do?
Mother has dementia, can't access her bank account
How to become a deputy in Singapore?
part_a_general_info: If a person has already lost mental capacity and has no LPA in place, you must apply to the Family Justice Courts for a Deputyship order under the Mental Capacity Act 2008. You will need a medical report certifying the loss of mental capacity from a qualified medical practitioner. A Deputy can be granted powers over Personal Welfare and/or Property & Affairs, similar to an LPA Donee. For smaller estates (generally under $60,000), a Simplified Track may apply, which is cheaper and faster. The Deputy must submit annual reports to the Office of the Public Guardian on the use of the person's funds.
triage_questions: Q1: Who has lost mental capacity? What is your relationship to them?
Q2: When and how was the loss of capacity identified?
Q3: Do they have an existing LPA?
Q4: What is the approximate total value of their assets?
Q5: Have other family members been consulted? Do they agree with your application?
branching_logic: If Q3 = LPA exists → No need for Deputyship. Activate the LPA.
If Q4 < $60,000 → Simplified Track may apply.
If Q5 = family disagrees → Contested application. More complex.
routing: Route A (No LPA, family agrees): Refer to PBSG clinic for Deputyship application. If estate <$60k, advise Simplified Track.
Route B (LPA exists): No Deputyship needed. Advise on activating the existing LPA via OPG.
Route C (Family disputes): Escalate to PBSG staff. Contested Deputyship may require legal representation.
guardrail: Must NOT prepare any Deputyship application or court documents.
